 New MBPP smart city study outlines building upgrades, flood monitoring
 Halim Yaacob / EdgeProp.my November 13, 2026 Updated: about 4 hours ago Add EdgeProp as preferred source MBPP’s smart city study report proposes building-efficiency upgrades, earlier flood warnings, responsive traffic signals and better-connected planning data. The measures outline a proposed rollout through 2030 and remain subject to implementation. Highlights only
 AI-powered summary, reviewed by our editors
 PETALING JAYA (Nov 13): A Penang Island City Council (MBPP) smart city study report proposes building-efficiency upgrades, integrated flood monitoring and urban data platforms to support planning and municipal services on Penang island.
 The MBPP Smart City Action Plan 2030 study report envisages starting with council-owned buildings as demonstration projects for smart energy and water meters, indoor air-quality monitoring, accessibility improvements and refurbishment works, before progressively extending requirements to new developments and major renovations.
 Its proposed implementation schedule lists smart metering requirements for new buildings in the fourth quarter of 2026, public-building retrofits by the fourth quarter of 2028, indoor air-quality monitoring by the fourth quarter of 2029, and energy and water performance dashboards by the second quarter of 2030.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 The municipal action plan was launched alongside Penang’s statewide Smart City Blueprint 2040 on Tuesday (Nov 10). Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the plans would strengthen data and technology integration and translate smart city aspirations into initiatives addressing residents’ needs.
 The detailed proposals are set out in the publicly available study report; whether all were retained unchanged in the edition launched on Nov 10 has not been confirmed. The report’s schedules are planning milestones and do not, by themselves, establish that requirements have taken effect or projects have secured funding, a Bernama report said.
 Building performance and flood resilience
 According to the study report, the building programme would use guidelines, planning conditions and incentives to encourage or require improvements in energy, water and environmental performance.
 Other built-environment proposals include an electric vehicle infrastructure master plan, additional space for public chargers, solar installations on public buildings and accessibility upgrades to priority public facilities.
 For disaster preparedness, the report proposes an integrated disaster and climate resilience monitoring platform, bringing together environmental and infrastructure data to support early detection, risk assessment and coordinated responses.
 Its proposed schedule lists flood and climate sensors by the second quarter of 2027, a real-time risk dashboard by the second quarter of 2028 and early-warning alert systems by the first quarter of 2029.
 At the launch, Chow said flooding, traffic congestion, solid waste management and rising urban temperatures required physical planning and integrated solutions alongside technology, according to state publication Buletin Mutiara .
 Connecting planning data and city operations
 A proposed urban observatory would consolidate information on population, housing, land use, infrastructure, mobility and environmental conditions, with analytical tools to support planning and policy evaluation.
 The study report lists the integration of spatial, socio-economic and infrastructure datasets by the third quarter of 2027, followed by a public analytics and open-data portal by the second quarter of 2028.
 A separate smart command centre initiative would use digital twins — virtual models of urban assets and systems — to monitor conditions and test responses to traffic congestion, flooding and utility disruptions. Priority models for traffic, floods and utilities are scheduled in the report for the first quarter of 2029.
 The proposals build on existing systems. The report identifies the Virtual Island of Penang platform as operational and describes MBPP’s Intelligent Operation Centre as a round-the-clock hub for monitoring urban operations.
 Feedback gathered during the study highlighted systems developed around individual departmental needs, with differing levels of integration. Other agencies called for existing platforms to be connected and improved rather than duplicated.
 At the state level, Chow identified the proposed Penang Urban Intelligence Observatory, data exchange platform and Smart Penang Dashboard as components intended to strengthen data integration and government decision-making.
 Mobility and delivery responsibilities
 For transport, the study report proposes adaptive traffic signal controls by the second quarter of 2027 and artificial intelligence-based congestion and incident detection by the second quarter of 2028.
 Its shared mobility programme includes cycling and micromobility corridors by the fourth quarter of 2027, shared mobility hubs by the fourth quarter of 2028, and first- and last-mile connectivity improvements by the fourth quarter of 2029.
 To coordinate delivery, the report proposes a Smart City Steering Committee for strategic oversight, a Smart City Management Office for central coordination, and department-led working groups responsible for projects, budgets and operational performance.
 The proposed monitoring framework includes monthly operational reporting, quarterly management reviews and publication of selected dashboard indicators quarterly or annually.
 State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the statewide blueprint, prepared by PLANMalaysia Penang, covers seven sectors: Smart People, Smart Living, Smart Environment, Smart Government, Smart Economy, Smart Mobility and Smart Digital Infrastructure.
 MBPP’s action plan focuses on municipal service efficiency, mobility management, digital infrastructure, environmental sustainability and community well-being, he said, according to Bernama .
